topology: 4 nodes x 1 rank x 1 H100, OpenMPI/HPC-X 2.16 over UCX over NDR InfiniBand
golden: none — assertions only. A third-party application's counts are not ours to freeze.
why: Plane-wave DFT is the first workload in this corpus that is neither a halo exchange nor a collective on a contiguous buffer. The FFT grid is distributed over planes, so the dominant primitive is MPI_ALLTOALL (FFTXlib/src/fft_scatter.f90:715, :792), and QE nests that all-to-all inside a communicator hierarchy whose partition of MPI_COMM_WORLD is pure arithmetic in Modules/mp_pools.f90:73-92. Changing -npool therefore changes the comm matrix in a way derivable from the source without naming a single rank — which is what makes it an assertion rather than a golden.
workload_note:
AUSURF112 from github.com/QEF/benchmarks, unmodified: 112 Au atoms, nbnd=800, ecutwfc=25 Ry, ecutrho=200 Ry, K_POINTS automatic 2 2 1 1 1 0 (=> 2 irreducible k-points, which is what makes -npool 2 legal), electron_maxstep=2 as the benchmark ships it. `iters` is SCF iterations, not messages: nothing here derives a message COUNT from it. QE's message counts depend on how many Davidson steps the diagonaliser takes, which is data-dependent, so every assertion in this case is about the SHAPE of the matrix and never about its volume. `npool` is the only difference between the two captures.

Note for anyone reusing this: tests/hpc/suite/sql_check.sh's PARAM_COLS allowlist has no slot for `npool`, so these assertions are driven by this case's own check.sh, which materialises `params` from the block above with no allowlist. See NOTES.md.
not_covered: No gpumem/p2p pass. NVBit costs ~8 minutes of module processing per run and pw.x is a 52 MB binary linking cuFFT, cuBLAS and cuSOLVER — the module-lift cost would dominate the allocation, and `p2p` is known-buggy (plans/PLAN-20260810-0854). The managed-memory question this case was chosen for is settled at the LINK line instead (see REPORT.md), which is where the evidence actually lives: mem_object carries no discriminator, so a gpumem capture could not have answered it either.
transport_note: Both captures that carry the -npool claim run on the DEFAULT UCX transport — QE exactly as a user runs it. An earlier revision pinned UCX_TLS=rc_verbs so ibv_post_send would fire; it aborted both runs (job 45082487) with ibv_reg_mr(...len=3409920) failed: Bad address / md[3]=mlx5_0 (md supports: host) / rndv.c:2360 assertion. pw.x is CUDA-aware and hands MPI GPU device pointers, and rc_verbs' memory domain is host-only, so UCX's rendezvous cannot register the user buffer. That is a fact about this application's reach, not a flag to tune, and it is not worked around in the claim-bearing captures. A separate bonus run (qe-npool1-rcverbs) retries rc_verbs with cuda_copy,gdr_copy and UCX_RNDV_THRESH=inf purely to test whether the wire can be made visible at all; it runs last and nothing in the report depends on it.

expect_fail_asserts.ucx_peer_matrix_is_recoverable: ucx_worker_address is empty on every OpenMPI point-to-point run: it is produced only from ucp_worker_get_address (providers/ucx/ucx_hooks.hpp:181), and HPC-X 2.16's mca_pml_ucx.so publishes its worker address through ucp_worker_query instead (login-node ELF sweep: pml_ucx's undefined symbols carry ucp_worker_query and ucp_worker_release_address but NOT ucp_worker_get_address; mca_osc_ucx.so and mca_spml_ucx.so carry both). So ucx_ep_connection.remote_prefix_hash — described in ucx_records.hpp:275-279 as the only row in the UCX family that crosses a rank boundary — points at nothing, and the UCX provider cannot produce a communication matrix for MPI point-to-point. Blocks PLAN-20260815-1540 stage 3's oracle. See REPORT.md finding 2.
expect_fail_asserts.endpoint_fanout_matches_pool_size: Counts messages where it should count bytes, and this application falsifies the proxy. At npool=2 every rank shows 2 heavy endpoints against the predicted 1; the capture shows why — rank 0's second endpoint carried 2,638 sends of 0/4/8/1024 B against 7,340 sends of 4,921,600 B on the first, i.e. control traffic, not data. Kept rather than deleted because the failure is a real property of the stack. The corrected claim is endpoint_fanout_by_bytes.sql, which measures the quantity the decomposition predicts; the independent reason for preferring bytes is ucx_records.hpp:80-90 and 19_ucx_mpi's workload_note, not this capture. NOT tuned to pass — the threshold is unchanged at 10 %. NOTE: check.sh keys expect_fail on the assertion NAME only, so this reports [XPASS] at npool=1. That XPASS is correct and expected — the count-based claim is true at npool=1 (3 heavy endpoints, 35%/35%/30%) and false at npool=2. Do not 'fix' the XPASS by weakening the assertion.

unanswerable_note: On the default transport ib_post_send and comm_edges are legitimately EMPTY: rc_mlx5 builds its WQEs and rings the doorbell inline, below every interposable verbs symbol, and connects its queue pairs through mlx5dv_devx_qp_modify rather than ibv_modify_qp. Assertions over those tables are therefore UNANSWERABLE in this configuration rather than false, and check.sh reports them as [skip] with the reason. They are kept, not deleted: the moment a transport or a provider makes that path observable they become live checks. ucx_and_verbs_agree_on_the_peer_set is in this class — with no verbs traffic to compare against, the two layers are not describing the same traffic and the question cannot be put.
oracle_note: fft_dense_nr3 (288) and fft_dense_sticks_total (11837) are pw.x's own numbers, printed before the SCF loop starts, and both are INDEPENDENT of -npool: pw.x prints the identical 'Dense grid: ... FFT dimensions (180, 90, 288)' and 'sticks: dense Sum 11837' at both rank divisions. They are fixed by the input file's cell and ecutrho, not by the run. What changes between the two captures — the per-peer transpose length — is DERIVED from them and params, which is what makes fft_transpose_message_size an oracle rather than a golden.
